sources.note: Vaiphei appears only in the Ethnologue-style list of Northern Kuki-Chin language names; no accent entry for it.

sources.citation: Suantak, Khawlsonkim. 2013. Vaiphei phonetics, phonology and morphology: a descriptive study. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, North-Eastern Hill University, Shillong. xi+284 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/169680.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 4 'Phonetics and Phonology' (pp. 65-132) covers inventory, distribution, contrasts, clusters, distinctive features, syllable/word structure (4.7), tone (4.8: 'Vaiphei is a tonal language... three contrastive tones, two contour tones (rising and falling) and a low tone', p.116; distribution p.119-121; tone sandhi p.122), vowel length (4.9) and VOT acoustics; no section, sentence or transcription convention for word stress/accent. The only 'stress' token is a generic definition in the Odden-style prosodic feature list (p.105: 'Stress: has greater emphasis, higher amplitude and pitc…
Phonology section (from Suantak 2013): consonants, vowels, three tones (21, 23, 52), tone sandhi, (C)V(C) syllable; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Lotven, Samson. 2023. Tone in South Central Tibeto-Burman (Kuki-Chin) [survey text held under reng1255].
sources.note: Cites Suantak 2013 only for Vaiphei tone facts (L on all syllable shapes, no contours before glottal stop, p.121; L -> Rise as first member of compound, p.122; tonal stem alternation). Nothing on Vaiphei stress.

sources.citation: Prichard, Jesse. 2018. Verb Stem Alternation in Vaiphei. MA thesis, Portland State University (Dissertations and Theses 4470). doi:10.15760/etd.6354. 94 pp.
sources.note: No word-stress statement. Only 'vocalic stress' within diphthongs after Button (2011): 'The vocalic stress in diphthongs of the cognate pia in Vaiphei matches that of Sizang and Thadou, but not that of Zo and Teddim' (p.58), i.e. which element of a diphthong is prominent; recommends a future 'study of vocalic stress assignment in Vaiphei' (p.7). Phonology otherwise taken from Suantak 2010/2013 (tones, phonotactics).

sources.citation: Yumnam, Satyabati Devi. 2010. A comparative phonology of Hmar, Paite and Vaiphei. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Manipur University. 271 pp. Shodhganga hdl 10603/105257 (scanned).
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. IV 'Inventory of Vaiphei phonemes' has 4.3 Syllable and 4.4 Tone only: 'Vaiphei has 2 (two) tones: (1) Level and (2) Falling. Only level tone is marked by (-)' (p.194); conclusion (p.226) repeats '2 suprasegmental phonemes are Level tone and Falling tone'. No stress/accent statement in TOC, tone/syllable pages or conclusion.
